name: wrocpp
description: Plugins that help Claude Code write C++ you would be happy to maintain, from the Wro.cpp community.

metadata.description: C++ plugins from Wro.cpp: C++26 reflection and idioms, quality gates, evidence-backed conventions, modules and fuzzing.

plugins.name: cpp26-guard
plugins.description: Keep C++26 free of hand-written copies of definitions. Skills reflect-dont-hand-write (derive enum names, name lookups, flag parsing and member lists with std::meta reflection, with a tested reference header and a GCC 16.2 evidence table) and cpp26-idioms (constrained templates, import std, std::format and std::print, one append instead of a chain, opt-in comment policy), advisory pre-write and post-write hooks, two tested lints with allowance files, configured by .claude/cpp26-guard.json.

plugins.name: cpp-quality-gates
plugins.description: Make 'done' mean measured for C++: skills for a sanitizer matrix (ASan, UBSan, TSan, LSan; Linux-in-a-container for macOS), a CRAP gate (lizard + gcovr), mutation testing (universalmutator harness with triage), and a compiler capability matrix, with runnable scripts, CMake presets and CI templates.

plugins.name: cpp-conventions
plugins.description: Evidence-backed C++ conventions as five skills - designated-init (one braced expression per value), no-needless-copies (views, sinks, ownership boundaries), cppreference (confirm a rule and cite the page, cached offline), units (std::chrono and mp-units quantities, one wall clock) and no-magic-numbers (name every number once) - with compiler fixtures for GCC and Clang and an advisory pre-write hook that scans new C++ text for copy smells and bare numbers.

plugins.name: cpp-modules
plugins.description: Use import std and named modules with CMake and GCC 16: the experimental gate, a working template project and the traps that cost hours, each reproduced by a fixture.

plugins.name: cpp-fuzzing
plugins.description: One property function reused by every kind of C++ check, as three skills and a working starter: one-property-many-checks (unit tests, AFL++ and compile-time undefined-behaviour checks share one constexpr property), compile-time-corpus-and-exhaustive (#embed corpus replay and bounded-exhaustive static_asserts with budget and memory guidance), afl-harness (replay-and-AFL++ harness, Docker recipe, time-boxed campaign, crash triage).

plugins.name: tidy-agent
plugins.description: Run clang-tidy on every C++ file the agent edits, and turn recurring agent mistakes into tested clang-tidy checks. Pre-release; lives in wrocpp/tidy-agent.
